extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers / creative writers thinking about narrative point-of-view
extracted.subtask_description: Practical advice for choosing and handling narrative point-of-view (POV) in fiction, describing modes (first/second/third/objective/omniscient), risks, mixing, and techniques to manage reader intimacy and information. Useful for novelists and short-story writers revising POV or deciding who tells the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know Thy Narrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify who tells the story before writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide the narrator up front—know the vantage and limits of the voice carrying the tale; this informs what information and tone are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who's On First, I Don't Know's On Third
rubrics_metrics.description: First-person uses "I"; third-person uses "she/he/they."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of pronoun choice because it defines basic perspective and the grammatical lens through which events are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-Person, That's A Good One (use cautiously)
rubrics_metrics.description: Second-person ("you") is risky.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second-person can be powerful but difficult to sustain and may alienate or confuse readers if mishandled; use deliberately and with awareness of its strangeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witnessing Versus Experiencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-person = witness; first-person = experiential immersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose third-person when you want some distance and observational tone; choose first-person when you want deep immersion and immediacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Intimacy Of The Reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Different POV modes create varying closeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how close you want the reader to feel to characters—POV choice affects emotional engagement and reader sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: The Reader At The Window
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective POV restricts readers from internal thoughts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective (dramatic) POV conveys only what can be observed—action, dialogue, and detail—leaving interpretation to readers; useful for restraint and showing rather than telling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjective: The Reader As A Psychic Monkey
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjective POV grants access to one character's interior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjective modes let you convey thoughts, feelings, and perceptions of a single character, shaping the reader's alignment and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omniscient: Reader Drops Acid
rubrics_metrics.description: Omniscient POV gives access to all characters' thoughts simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omniscience can offer panoramic insight but risks confusing or flattening perspective; use voice and authorial commentary carefully to maintain coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Limited Lens Of Third Person Subjective
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-person subjective = witness perspective plus intimate access to one mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this when you want the flexibility of third-person narration with the closeness of a single-character interior—keeps some observational distance while still delivering character depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episodic Third: Monkey Hops From Shoulder To Shoulder
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter-by-chapter character shifts (episodic third-person).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifting the focal character by section or chapter can broaden perspective across the work, but each shift should be clear and motivated to avoid reader confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Deeper Plunge Of First Person Subjective
rubrics_metrics.description: First-person subjective offers a deeper plunge; risk: narrator voice indistinguishable from author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-person delivers strong immediacy and personality but requires a distinct, consistent voice to avoid the narrator reading like the author's own voice or becoming flat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: The News Report Had Sex With A Screenplay
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective POV: details, actions, dialogue, no interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective prose resembles a report or script—relay sensory facts and let readers infer motivations and internal states from observable behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Person Omniscient
rubrics_metrics.description: First-person omniscient exists but requires justification (ghost, psychic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a first-person narrator knows things beyond their experience, you must supply a credible reason (supernatural ability, later knowledge, authorial device) so it doesn't break trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple First Person Narrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple first-person narrators: each voice must be distinctive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using multiple first-person voices, ensure each narrator has a clearly different voice, perspective, and reason for telling the story to avoid blending and reader fatigue.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Cool Kids Of POV High
rubrics_metrics.description: First-person subjective and third-person limited episodic dominate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These POV choices are common and effective; consider them as strong default options while being mindful of their conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: First And Third Living Together
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixing first and third requires logical justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you switch between first and third within a work, provide structural or narrative reasons for the change so it feels purposeful rather than arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Consistent, Be Clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain POV choices throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inconsistencies or unclear shifts in POV will confuse readers—establish the narrative vantage and stick to its rules unless you deliberately break them with clear signaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Reader Is Your Puppet And POV Is One Of The Strings
rubrics_metrics.description: POV is a manipulative tool controlling information access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use POV to manage what the reader knows and when—it's a primary technique for pacing, surprise, and controlling sympathy or judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspective Creates Tension
rubrics_metrics.description: Restricting or revealing information via perspective generates suspense and dramatic irony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate withholding or disclosure from the chosen POV creates emotional stakes and can produce irony when readers know more than characters (or vice versa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wuzza Wooza Who Now?
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware confusing readers through excessive omniscience or subjectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too much jumping between minds or too broad an omniscience can disorient readers; balance perspective breadth with clarity and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Danger Of Illuminating Assholes
rubrics_metrics.description: Intimate POV with morally questionable characters is tricky.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing very close to an unlikeable or immoral character risks endorsing them or alienating readers—craft voice and framing carefully to maintain reader engagement and critical distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Objectivity Misses
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectivity sacrifices the novel's unique power to explore inner experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing an objective stance may forgo deep interiority and the opportunity to render subjective emotional truth; weigh this loss against the strengths of restraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is The Narrator A Lying Liar?
rubrics_metrics.description: Unreliable narrators work best with intimate POV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unreliability is most effective when readers are close enough to the narrator to notice discrepancies between perception and reality; intimacy enhances the deceptive or partial view.

rubrics_metrics.name: This Is All Wrapped Up With Narrative Tense
rubrics_metrics.description: POV plus tense create additional variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how tense (past, present) interacts with POV to affect immediacy, memory, and trustworthiness; both choices alter reader experience and should be coherent with voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: When In Doubt, Rewrite To A New POV
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimentation with POV can revitalize a struggling manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a scene or manuscript isn't working, trying it in a different POV can reveal new possibilities—rewriting POV is a practical revision tactic.
